title: Deterministic Verification and a Single‑Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the identical LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation call per intent that is reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we produced N = 250 natural-language intents with gpt-5-mini and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated template repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 initial generations + 1 repair). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the reported estimand and inference apply to the synthetic/emulation partition only. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived as described in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work documents LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A widely adopted architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. These pipelines reduce mechanically checkable error classes (syntax, simple ordering and local-policy violations) but leave open questions about their marginal benefit when LLM outputs are already highly conformant under constrained task regimes.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal verifier+single-repair effect when the same initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). By design the experiment measures only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. Our principal contribution is the concrete, artifact-grounded quantification of that marginal effect (with exact counts, confidence intervals, and reconciled provider-accounting) for a constrained NetOps task set.
sections.related_work:
Representative surveys and empirical studies motivate generate–verify architectures and evaluation practices. Prior NetOps-focused and LLM-survey material documents that (a) LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled setups [1],[2]; (b) deterministic verification tools and header-space/model-checking techniques provide mechanized checks for forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are commonly used as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[5]; and (c) generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows increase detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects in code and configuration domains, while deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties remain challenging [4],[6].

Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval-based threats emphasize the need for filtering and validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines but note that adaptive adversaries remain an unresolved operational threat [7].

This study differs from prior reports by (i) using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical generated candidates, (ii) reporting complete provider-call accounting and deterministic reconciliation for stage-level modeling of generation and repair calls, and (iii) archiving comprehensive validator traces and reconciliation artifacts so that the exact numeric outcomes and stage mappings are auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and specified a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion rules, analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and the maximum model-call budget. The preregistration artifact is archived with the study identifier recorded in the Evidence Bundle referenced below.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider-call reconciliation (explicit). Under the registered shared_initial_candidate design exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and that same generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded); independent first-pass generations per condition were not performed. Provider accounting reconciles the execution to hosted model calls = 251: 250 initial-generation calls plus 1 repair-stage call. The adapter records stage_counts corresponding to 250 shared initial generations and 1 repair stage; adapter labeling maps condition_counts labeled by the adapter (e.g., entries labeled "shared" and "guarded") to these stage-level events. This mapping explains why condition-level labels in the audit can appear to show "shared":250 and "guarded":1 while the executed stages were 250 shared_initial_generation events and one repair event. We report the numeric decomposition (250 initial + 1 repair = 251 model calls) so readers can precisely interpret the adapter accounting.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). Tasks exercised workflow constraints (make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe access transfer patterns) and protected interfaces; full task manifest entries are archived in the evidence bundle.

Model invocation policy and guarded pipeline. The declared model used for all initial shared generations was gpt-5-mini. For each intent we executed one shared initial generation call. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, counting parsed_command_count, checking required_sequence ordering, validating workflow constraints (group-activity and make-before-break rules), and comparing the resulting final_state snapshot to the expected_final_state encoded in the task payload. When the validator returned valid = false for a guarded episode, the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair attempt (syntactic/ordering fixes only) and re-submitted the repaired candidate to the validator. No multi-iteration repair or human escalation was permitted by design.

Inclusion and contamination rules. The preregistered exclusion rules removed items whose vendor-parsers deterministically prevented verification, or items containing credential-like tokens or denylist hits. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens or private-address artifacts; flagged items would be excluded from the primary analysis and treated in sensitivity analyses. In this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged.

Analysis plan. Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1. The primary test is an exact two-sided McNemar on the paired outcomes; we also computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded minus baseline paired difference using 10,000 resamples. Secondary and sensitivity analyses (missing-pair treatments, contamination-as-failure) were preregistered and archived.
sections.results:
Execution and raw counts. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 initial generations + 1 repair). Provider-call accounting reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus the single repair-stage call.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (1.0). Observed paired contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair call; repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). These numbers and bootstrap parameters are recorded in the archived analysis artifacts.

Representative validator diagnostics and repair. Validator traces for passed episodes include parsed_command_count matching the required_sequence size and valid = true. For the sole failing baseline candidate the single permitted template repair produced a syntactic/ordering adjustment sufficient to satisfy the validator; both the repair trace and the guarded scoring artifact for that pair are archived.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination. No episodes were excluded from the primary confirmatory analysis: complete_pairs = 250 and all other missingness counts = 0. Contamination detectors flagged no confirmatory episodes, so no sensitivity-treatment exclusions were required for the primary estimand.
sections.discussion:
Operational meaning of the observed near-null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the lone failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the possible verifier-improvement under this pipeline and task scope.

Why the observed gain was small. Artifact-grounded factors explain the small observed gain: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) the declared model produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshots) and does not capture broader behavioral correctness in live protocol execution or cross-device emergent interactions.

Power, assumptions, and interpretation. The preregistration power calculation assumed baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15 percentage-point absolute effect with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed and reduces the ability to detect small absolute improvements; accordingly, the paired-bootstrap CI bounding the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement is the most informative inferential output.

Scope and external validity. Internal validity is tied to prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the precise validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but not live protocol-level correctness. External validity: confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised and remain an unresolved threat.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitted at most one automated repair per episode as specified in the preregistration. Execution accounting reported planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 initial shared generations + 1 repair).

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: preregistration id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration artifact archived in the evidence bundle). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Evidence bundle pointer: the full execution and analysis manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis outputs referenced in this manuscript are archived and available in the run's evidence bundle (see the execution manifest file in the archived bundle for the full manifest). The manuscript reports numeric reconciliation facts (e.g., model_calls_used decomposition, stage_counts, contingency counts, bootstrap parameters) that are reproducible from the archived manifests.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
